name: DroPE — Dropping the Positional Embeddings after pretraining
aka: 'RoPE as a training scaffold'; post-hoc NoPE conversion. NOT DRoPE = Directional RoPE (2503.15029, driving-agent modelling, unrelated)

source.title: Extending the Context of Pretrained LLMs by Dropping Their Positional Embeddings (the abstract names the method DroPE)
source.authors: Gelberg, Eguchi, Akiba, Cetin (Sakana AI / Oxford)
source.evidence: [v1] Sat, 13 Dec 2025 04:23:47 UTC (PDF footer 'arXiv:2512.12167v1 [cs.CL] 13 Dec 2025'); public launch (blog sakana.ai/drope, code, HF checkpoints) 12 Jan 2026

secondary.label: Sakana AI blog + code + checkpoints (public launch)
Homonym to avoid: DRoPE — Directional Rotary Position Embedding (unrelated)

firstShipped.model: Sakana's own recalibrated Llama-2-7b-hf-DroPE checkpoint (SmolLM recipes ship as configs only); no frontier model as of Aug 2026

problem: RoPE models collapse past their pretraining length. Zero-shot scaling (PI, NTK, YaRN, LongRoPE2) keeps perplexity by compressing low frequencies — but the paper shows this warps the semantic-attention heads so the model effectively *crops* far-away tokens. And the standard fix, long-context fine-tuning, is quadratic-cost and needs long data. NoPE from scratch converges more slowly and ends worse (bounded positional-bias gradients at init).
idea: Treat the positional encoding as a transient training aid. Pretrain with RoPE (it accelerates convergence), then delete it from every layer — the model becomes NoPE, position available only through the causal mask — and briefly continue pretraining at the *original* length so the network re-learns its induction heads without explicit PE. There is now no out-of-distribution positional signal at longer lengths, so it extrapolates zero-shot — with one inference-time knob: a softmax logit scale (β* ≈ 1 + 0.4·ln s from scratch, 1 + 0.1·ln s for SmolLM) tuned on a held-out set at the target length.
buys: Zero-shot 2–8×+ context: 0.5B model NIAH at 2× 28.0 / 41.6 / 23.3 (multi-query/key/value) vs YaRN 17.8 / 0.5 / 14.6; SmolLM-360M NIAH at 8× 52.2% vs LongRoPE2 16.45%; LongBench Llama-2-7B 26.08 vs NTK 21.88 / YaRN 19.14
>95% of short-context performance recovered after <5B recalibration tokens (0.8% of a 600B budget); can be folded into a pretraining recipe at zero extra cost (drop RoPE for the last ~12% of tokens)
Closes the loop the timeline opened in 2021: positions were the lever, now they are the scaffold
costs: Not an inference-time knob: needs the weights and a training run on pretraining-distribution data (2B tokens for 0.5B; ~20B for 7B) — useless with API-only access
Absolute long-context scores remain low (multi-key NIAH 41.6% at 2×; Llama-2-7B LongBench avg 26) — 'far better than YaRN zero-shot' is not 'solved'; evidence is ≤7B

Timing matters (dropping too early hurts final perplexity); the long-context numbers use a tuned logit-scale knob at inference — the same kind of heuristic SWAN and Llama 4 lean on; QK-Norm was needed only for the high-LR SmolLM-360M recalibrations; unproven at 1M-token agent scale

chatbot2k.why: zero benefit if you never leave training length

rag32k.why: pretrained at 4K, want 32K NIAH/QA without long-context fine-tuning — if you own the pipeline

coding128k.why: 2–8× zero-shot might reach 128K, but absolute recall stays low and you need the weights

agent1m.why: unproven; prefer long-context training + hybrid attention

pickWhen.verdict: It buys zero-shot extension for ~1% of pretraining compute and sells nothing on the compute/KV bill. Right if you train; wrong if you only serve.

name: HySparse — hybrid sparse attention with oracle token selection and KV sharing

source.title: HySparse: A Hybrid Sparse Attention Architecture with Oracle Token Selection and KV Cache Sharing

oneLiner: Interleave each full-attention layer with several sparse layers whose token selection and KV cache are derived from the preceding full layer — sparsity that borrows the exact layer's judgement.
whyFootnote: Research-scale hybrid; represented on the timeline by NSA / DSA / DeepSeek-V4.

name: Neural Attention Search Linear (NAtS-L) — token-level linear / softmax hybrid

source.title: Neural Attention Search Linear: Towards Adaptive Token-Level Hybrid Attention Models

oneLiner: Linear attention and softmax attention inside the same layer, on different tokens, chosen per token — the hybrid at token rather than layer granularity.
whyFootnote: Research-scale; the layer-level hybrids are the nodes.

name: MiniCPM-SALA — sparse (InfLLM-V2) + linear (Lightning) attention in one 9B model

source.title: MiniCPM-SALA: Hybridizing Sparse and Linear Attention for Efficient Long-Context Modeling
source.evidence: HF README: '[2026.02.11] MiniCPM-SALA is released!' (repo created 2026-02-11); '25% of the layers adopt InfLLM-V2 and the remaining 75% utilize Lightning Attention', HyPE positional embedding, converted from dense weights at ~25% of a from-scratch budget; arXiv API published 2026-02-12T09:37:05Z (v1)

problem: Sparse attention keeps long-context fidelity but still pays for the whole cache; linear attention is cheap but blurs. Can one small model take both?
idea: A 9B hybrid converted from a dense model at ~25% of a from-scratch budget: a quarter of the layers trainable sparse attention (InfLLM-V2), three quarters Lightning (linear) attention, with HyPE (RoPE on the linear layers, NoPE on the attention layers) — the 'attend to few' and 'remember cheaply' threads in one stack.
buys: The two efficiency threads literally merged in one architecture, at a size you can run locally
costs: 9B research release; the ratio and the linear/sparse split are tuned choices; long-context recall evidence is the team's own

chatbot2k.why: sparse and linear layers both save nothing a 2K prompt is paying

rag32k.why: the InfLLM-V2 quarter keeps retrieval fidelity, but three quarters blur; 9B, team's own evidence

agent1m.why: the right shape for 1M, but a 9B research release with the team's own recall evidence

pickWhen.verdict: A footnote-sized model making the timeline's point: sparse for the exact layers, linear for the rest.

name: Qwen3.5-397B-A17B — Gated DeltaNet hybrid at flagship scale (45 linear : 15 full)

source.title: Qwen3.5-397B-A17B (Hugging Face model repo)
source.evidence: HF repo createdAt 2026-02-16T04:55:12Z; config.json: 60 layers, layer_types 45 linear_attention : 15 full_attention, full_attention_interval 4, 32 Q / 2 KV heads (head 256), linear 64 V / 16 K heads × 128, max_position_embeddings 262144

problem: Take the Qwen3-Next recipe from an 80B experiment to the flagship: 262K context served cheaply at 397B total / 17B active.
idea: 15 × (3 × (Gated DeltaNet → MoE) → 1 × (Gated Attention → MoE)) — the same 3:1 layout, now the family's main model.
buys: The delta rule is no longer an experiment: a frontier family's flagship runs 75% of its layers on a fixed-size state
Gated (sink-free) attention on the exact layers
costs: Still 1/4 layers full-attention KV; recall on the linear layers is bounded; hybrid KV managers and FLA kernels are required to serve it

rag32k.why: the throughput win is at long context; at 32K bounded linear-layer recall is the trade

coding128k.why: 262K native covers 128K; three quarters of layers hold a fixed-size state, decode cheap

agent1m.why: the recipe was built for this

pickWhen.verdict: The 2025 hybrid became a 2026 default. Nothing new in the mechanism — the news is who is running it.

name: DeepSeek-V4 — Compressed Sparse Attention + Heavily Compressed Attention

source.title: DeepSeek-V4 Preview Release (news); tech report 'DeepSeek-V4: Towards Highly Efficient Million-Token Context Intelligence'
source.evidence: DeepSeek news page (URL slug news260424; the fetched page header read 'DeepSeek-V4 Preview Release 2026/04/24' — the body copy itself carries no other date) — 'Novel Attention: Token-wise compression + DSA (DeepSeek Sparse Attention)', '1M context is now the default'; open weights on HF the same day; arXiv API for 2606.19348v1: published 2026-04-26T14:49:33Z (the identifier's YYMM prefix does not match the recorded April submission — recorded as the API returns it)

secondary.label: Tech report, arXiv 2606.19348 (abstract: 27% of single-token FLOPs and 10% of KV cache vs V3.2 at 1M)
FlashMemory-DeepSeek-V4: lookahead sparse attention on the lightning index (third-party)
GLM-5.2 'IndexShare' — one lightning indexer reused across four sparse layers (Jun 2026)

firstShipped.model: DeepSeek-V4-Pro (1.6T/49B) and V4-Flash (284B/13B), open weights, 1M context default

problem: DSA made attention O(L·k), but at 1M tokens the cache still holds a million latent entries per layer and the indexer still scans them all. Wanted 1M as the *default* for every service, at a fraction of V3.2's per-token FLOPs and KV.
idea: Two layer types, interleaved. **CSA:** compress the KV of every m tokens into one entry with a learned token-level compressor (weighted average with learned weights and positional biases), then run DSA — the lightning indexer picks the top-k *compressed* entries per query — plus a sliding-window branch over recent uncompressed KV for local detail. **HCA:** a much larger compression rate m′ ≫ m and dense, MQA-style attention over *all* compressed entries, for layers that tolerate more approximation. RoPE only on the last 64 dims.
buys: At 1M context, V4-Pro needs 27% of V3.2's single-token inference FLOPs and 10% of its KV cache (V4-Flash: 10% of the FLOPs); 1M context 'now the default across all official DeepSeek services'
The shape the timeline predicts, shipped at frontier scale: compress, then select, then attend — NSA's compress branch and DSA's select branch in one design
Open weights (MIT) at 1.6T / 49B active and 284B / 13B active
costs: Compression is lossy by construction: fine-grained recall beyond the sliding window depends on the compressor keeping what matters — the report's own evals, no independent long-context audit yet as of Aug 2026
The report deliberately omits m, m′, k, the window and the CSA:HCA layer ratio ('refer to our open-source implementation'), so the design is only fully specified in code
Two new layer types + a compressor + an indexer = more kernels and serving complexity; still an interleaved hybrid, so some layers pay more than others

rag32k.why: lossy compression buys little at 32K and risks fine-grained recall beyond the sliding window

coding128k.why: if you are training at this scale

agent1m.why: the design was built for 1M-token defaults

pickWhen.verdict: The most literal 'pay less of the bill' entry on the timeline: the exact layers no longer read tokens, they read a few compressed entries chosen by an index.

name: FlashMemory-DeepSeek-V4 — lookahead sparse attention on the lightning index

source.title: FlashMemory-DeepSeek-V4: Lightning Index Ultra-Long Context via Lookahead Sparse Attention

oneLiner: Third-party extension of DeepSeek-V4's index for ultra-long contexts via lookahead sparse selection.

name: Kimi K3 — Kimi Delta Attention 3:1 with gated MLA at 2.8T (69 KDA + 24 gated MLA layers), plus Attention Residuals

source.title: Kimi K3 (blog + Hugging Face model card); technical report 'Kimi K3: Open Frontier Intelligence'
source.evidence: HF blog: 'publicly released Kimi K3 on July 16, 2026, with full open-source weights promised by July 27'; HF card: 'built on Kimi Delta Attention (KDA) and Attention Residuals (AttnRes)', 'Layers: 93 (69 KDA + 24 Gated MLA)', 1,048,576 context; kimi.com/blog/kimi-k3 (page undated on-page); report arXiv API published 2026-07-27T16:49:54Z (v1)

firstShipped.model: Kimi K3 (2.8T / 104B active, 1M context, open weights)

problem: Serve a 1M-token context at 2.8T parameters; the Kimi Linear recipe was proven at 48B.
idea: 93 layers: 69 KDA (channel-wise gated delta rule) and 24 gated MLA layers, roughly 3:1; Attention Residuals let each layer attend over the outputs of earlier layers instead of summing them uniformly.
buys: KDA at the largest open scale yet; the report claims ~2.5× scaling efficiency over K2 and ~75% less KV than full attention
costs: Prefix caching had to be re-engineered for KDA (Moonshot contributed a vLLM implementation); 1/4 layers still full MLA; the report's own evals

chatbot2k.why: a 2.8T 3:1 KDA hybrid to save KV a 2K prompt never spends

rag32k.why: ~75% less KV matters little at 32K; retrieval leans on the quarter of gated MLA layers

coding128k.why: well inside the 1M it serves; KDA layers hold fixed state, the MLA quarter carries recall

pickWhen.verdict: The delta rule's biggest ship so far — 5½ years after Schlag, Irie and Schmidhuber.

name: qTTT — query-only test-time training for long context

source.title: Let's (not) just put things in Context: Test-Time Training for Long-Context LLMs

oneLiner: Diagnoses 'score dilution' in static softmax at long context; caches K/V once, then takes a few gradient steps on the query projections only before answering.
whyFootnote: Research-scale; the TTT line is represented by TTT-E2E.

name: TTT-E2E — end-to-end test-time training for long context

source.title: End-to-End Test-Time Training for Long Context

problem: A fixed-size state forgets; a KV cache grows. Can the model's own weights be the long-term memory, updated while it reads?
idea: A standard Transformer with sliding-window attention whose MLP layers keep learning at inference by next-token prediction on the context; the initialisation for that test-time learning is meta-learned during pretraining, and a static second MLP is kept as safe storage.
buys: Context beyond the window lives in weights, not in a cache — memory per token is constant
The Titans / test-time-training thread with an end-to-end recipe
costs: Gradient steps at inference (compute, kernels, batching complexity); evidence at research scale; recall depends on what the fast weights keep

chatbot2k.why: gradient steps at inference to remember beyond a window a 2K prompt never leaves

rag32k.why: retrieval needs exact recall; fast weights keep an uncertain subset, at research scale

coding128k.why: constant memory per token tempts at 128K; cross-file recall depends on what weights retain

pickWhen.verdict: The 'memory as weights trained at test time' line, made end-to-end — watch it, do not ship it yet.

name: HALO / HypeNet + HyPE — distil a Transformer into a 3:1 linear:softmax hybrid; RoPE on RNN layers, NoPE on attention layers

source.title: Hybrid Linear Attention Done Right: Efficient Distillation and Effective Architectures for Extremely Long Contexts

problem: Hybrids work but are trained from scratch; and which layer type should carry position?
idea: HALO converts a pretrained Transformer (Qwen3 1.7B–8B) into a 3:1 Lightning-linear : softmax hybrid with ~2.3B tokens; HypeNet adds HyPE — RoPE inside the recurrent layers, NoPE on the attention layers — plus dynamic logit scaling and QK-Norm.
buys: Retrofit-ability for hybrids: 2.3B tokens instead of a pretraining run
A clean answer to 'who carries position in a hybrid': the recurrent layers
costs: Research scale (≤8B); the linear layers keep the usual recall limits; the logit-scaling knob at long context

chatbot2k.why: a 2.3B-token conversion to save KV a 2K prompt does not have

rag32k.why: linear layers keep the usual recall limits; one softmax layer in four does retrieval

coding128k.why: you have a dense model and want a cheap hybrid

agent1m.why: research scale (≤8B) plus a logit-scaling knob at long context; 1M is untested

pickWhen.verdict: The recipe MiniCPM-SALA used; the timeline's 'retrofit-ability' prediction in one paper.

name: Token Sparse Attention — interleaved token selection with per-head Q/K/V compression

source.title: Token Sparse Attention: Efficient Long-Context Inference with Interleaved Token Selection

oneLiner: Compress per-head Q/K/V to a reduced token set inside attention and decompress the output, so dropped tokens can be reconsidered in later layers; drop-in with existing kernels.
whyFootnote: Research-scale; represented by the sparse-selection nodes.

name: GLM-5 adopts DeepSeek Sparse Attention; GLM-5.2 adds IndexShare (one indexer per four sparse layers)

source.title: GLM-5 (Hugging Face model card); report 'GLM-5: from Vibe Coding to Agentic Engineering'
source.evidence: HF repo created 2026-02-11T04:55:46Z; README: 'GLM-5 also integrates DeepSeek Sparse Attention (DSA)'; report arXiv API published 2026-02-17T17:50:56Z (v1); GLM-5.2 repo created 2026-06-16, README: 'We propose IndexShare, which reuses the [indexer] across every four sparse-attention layers'

firstShipped.model: GLM-5 (744B / 40B active, 200K, MIT) — the first major external adoption of DSA

problem: DSA was DeepSeek's; would anyone else pay the kernel and training cost to adopt it?
idea: Swap GLM-4.x's dense GQA for DSA's lightning indexer + top-k selection; four months later GLM-5.2 amortises the indexer — the term that dominates at 1M — by sharing one indexer across every four sparse layers.
buys: Content-based sparse attention crosses lab boundaries; IndexShare attacks the indexer's O(L²) directly
costs: Inherits DSA's fixed k and indexer scan; the report's own numbers

chatbot2k.why: inherits DSA's fixed k and indexer scan; both are pure overhead at 2K

rag32k.why: fixed k as DSA against only 32K keys; the indexer scan buys little

coding128k.why: the DSA 128K serving-cost cut, now with a second lab's kernels and training behind it

pickWhen.verdict: The moment DSA stopped being a DeepSeek trick and became a layer other labs pick.

name: Memory Caching — RNNs with growing memory

source.title: Memory Caching: RNNs with Growing Memory

oneLiner: Cache hidden-state checkpoints of a recurrent model so effective memory grows with length — a dial between fixed-state RNNs (O(1)) and Transformers (O(L) KV).

name: Multi-Head Low-Rank Attention (MLRA) — MLA with partitionable latents

source.title: Multi-Head Low-Rank Attention

oneLiner: Latent KV like MLA, but the latent can be partitioned across heads/devices — tensor-parallel decoding without replicating the cache (MLA's known awkwardness).

name: Mamba-3 — exponential-trapezoidal discretisation, complex state, MIMO SSM

source.title: Mamba-3: Improved Sequence Modeling using State Space Principles
source.authors: Lahoti, Li et al. (CMU / Together / Cartesia)
source.evidence: arXiv API published 2026-03-16T17:30:08Z (v1); ICLR 2026; Together AI blog 17 Mar 2026

problem: Mamba-2 traded expressivity for tensor-core friendliness (scalar decay); decode is memory-bound and the state cannot track order.
idea: An inference-first redesign: exponential-trapezoidal discretisation for a more expressive gated recurrence, a complex-valued (RoPE-like, data-dependent rotation) state for state tracking, and a multi-input multi-output SSM to raise arithmetic intensity at decode.
buys: Better quality per state size than Mamba-2 at matched compute; decode that uses the hardware
costs: Research scale; the SSM thread still trails softmax on exact recall; new kernels

chatbot2k.why: a fixed-size state and MIMO decode save nothing on a 2K KV cache

rag32k.why: the SSM still trails softmax on exact recall, which is what retrieval QA tests

coding128k.why: cheap decode, but exact cross-file recall is where the SSM thread still trails; research scale

agent1m.why: as the cheap layer of a hybrid

pickWhen.verdict: The SSM thread's 2026 step — three years after Mamba, still converging on the same hybrid shape.

name: Attention Residuals — softmax attention over depth replaces the fixed residual sum

source.title: Attention Residuals
source.evidence: arXiv API published 2026-03-16T09:32:21Z (v1); GitHub MoonshotAI/Attention-Residuals; used in Kimi K3 (Jul 2026)

problem: Residual connections sum every earlier layer with unit weight; deep models accumulate rather than select.
idea: Each layer attends — softmax with learned, input-dependent weights — over the outputs of preceding layers instead of summing them; a block variant attends over block-level representations to cap memory and communication.
buys: Attention applied along depth, not just sequence; shipped at 2.8T in Kimi K3
costs: Extra depth-wise attention cost and memory for earlier layer outputs (the block variant exists to bound it); a quality mechanism, not a bill item

chatbot2k.why: a quality mechanism, not a bill item; extra depth-wise attention cost even at 2K

rag32k.why: orthogonal to context length; helps selection over depth, not retrieval over 32K keys

coding128k.why: adds memory for earlier layer outputs on top of 128K KV; the block variant bounds it

agent1m.why: shipped in Kimi K3, but it buys quality; the block variant only bounds its own overhead

pickWhen.verdict: Not on the compute/KV bill at all — attention as a general selection operator, turned sideways.

name: Gemma 4 — 5:1 sliding window : global, p-RoPE on global layers, unified K/V and a cross-layer shared KV cache

source.title: Gemma 4 model card; Gemma 4 Technical Report
source.evidence: Google open-source blog 'Thursday, April 2, 2026'; model card: 'a hybrid attention mechanism that interleaves local sliding window attention with full global attention', 'global layers feature unified Keys and Values, and apply Proportional RoPE (p-RoPE)', windows 512 (E2B/E4B) / 1024, 4:1 (E2B) or 5:1 local:global; report arXiv API published 2026-07-02T21:08:53Z (v1)

problem: Gemma 3's 5:1 local:global bounded most of the cache; the global layers still paid full KV and full-frequency RoPE.
idea: Keep 5:1 (4:1 for E2B) with 512/1024 windows and a global final layer; on the global layers use unified Keys and Values (keys reused as values), share the KV cache across layers, and apply proportional RoPE — the lowest frequencies truncated (Barbero et al. 2024) — while local layers keep standard RoPE.
buys: Three KV cuts stacked on the global layers (unified K/V, cross-layer sharing, windows elsewhere); p-RoPE at scale as the answer to 'which frequencies extrapolate'
costs: Global layers still O(L); unified K/V is a quality trade the report has to defend; the recipe is Google's — configs are the source of truth

rag32k.why: the Gemma 3 recipe with the global layers' KV cut again; nothing to lose at 32K

pickWhen.verdict: Gemma 2 → 3 → 4: the same interleave, with more of the global-layer bill removed each generation.

name: Preconditioned DeltaNet — curvature-aware delta rule (unifies DeltaNet / GDN / KDA)

source.title: Preconditioned DeltaNet: Curvature-aware Sequence Modeling for Linear Recurrences

oneLiner: Adds a diagonal preconditioner to the delta rule's online-gradient update and derives DeltaNet, Gated DeltaNet and KDA as special cases, with chunkwise kernels.

name: Kwai Summary Attention (KSA) — learnable summary tokens compress history

source.title: Kwai Summary Attention Technical Report

oneLiner: Compress history into learnable summary tokens (O(n/k) retained entries) that later tokens attend to.
whyFootnote: Compression variant; DeepSeek-V4's CSA is the node.

name: Gated DeltaNet-2 — decoupled channel-wise erase and write gates

source.title: Gated DeltaNet-2: Decoupling Erase and Write in Linear Attention

problem: The delta rule ties erasing to writing through one scalar β; KDA made forgetting channel-wise but kept that coupling.
idea: A channel-wise erase gate and a separate channel-wise write gate on top of the gated delta rule; collapses to KDA when both gates share one scalar and to Gated DeltaNet when the decay collapses too.
buys: Finer control of what a fixed-size state forgets and keeps, with the same chunkwise-parallel training
costs: Still a bounded state; more gates, more kernel work; research scale so far

chatbot2k.why: a bounded-state layer whose extra gates buy nothing when the KV cache is 2K

rag32k.why: finer forgetting helps, but the state is still bounded and retrieval wants exact recall

coding128k.why: still a bounded state for cross-file recall; more gates, more kernel work, research scale

agent1m.why: the next step of the layer Qwen3.5 / Kimi K3 already ship

pickWhen.verdict: The 1960 delta rule keeps getting one more knob — 2021 β, 2024 α, 2025 per-channel, 2026 erase ≠ write.

name: MiniMax Sparse Attention (MSA) — MiniMax M3 returns to efficient attention, block-sparse over GQA

source.title: MiniMax M3 (blog); paper 'MiniMax Sparse Attention'
source.evidence: minimax.io/blog/minimax-m3 dated June 1, 2026 ('MiniMax Sparse Attention (MSA)'); HF MiniMaxAI/MiniMax-M3 repo created 2026-06-02; arXiv API published 2026-06-11T14:23:41Z (v1)

secondary.label: Context: 'Why did M2 end up as a full attention model?' (Oct 2025) — the retreat this reverses

problem: MiniMax had walked back its linear hybrid in M2 (Oct 2025) — infra maturity, eval blind spots. Eight months later the 1M-token bill was still there.
idea: Block-sparse attention on a GQA backbone: a lightweight index branch scores KV blocks and picks the top-k independently per GQA group; the main branch runs exact block-sparse attention over the selected uncompressed blocks with a fixed budget of 2,048 KV tokens per query.
buys: The lab that retreated from linear attention comes back via sparse selection — the 'attend to few' thread winning a convert from the 'remember cheaply' thread
GQA-friendly: selection per KV group, no MLA required
costs: Fixed 2K budget; block granularity; the indexer's cost at 1M; MiniMax's own evals

chatbot2k.why: a fixed 2,048-token budget covers a 2K prompt outright; the index branch is pure overhead

rag32k.why: selecting 2,048 of 32K is a modest cut; block granularity may miss needle passages

coding128k.why: exact attention over selected uncompressed blocks on a GQA backbone, no MLA retrofit needed

agent1m.why: the 1M bill is M3's stated target; the indexer's cost there is the trade

pickWhen.verdict: The most telling 2026 data point on the timeline: linear was abandoned, sparse was adopted — same bill, different lever.

name: Dynamic Linear Attention (DLA) — adaptive multi-state merging

source.title: Dynamic Linear Attention

oneLiner: Multi-state linear attention whose state boundaries move with information change, merging low-information states to keep a fixed-size chronological cache.

name: RoVE — Rotary Value Embeddings

source.title: RoVE: Rotary Value Embeddings Attention for Relative Position-dependent Value Pathways

oneLiner: Rotate the values too, so the value pathway is relative-position-sensitive; RoPE attention becomes an 'attentive convolution'.

name: HiLS — Hierarchical Landmark Sparse Attention

source.title: Hierarchical Sparse Attention Done Right: Toward Infinite Context Modeling

oneLiner: Chunk selection learned end-to-end under the LM loss via landmark tokens; each query attends to each retrieved chunk separately and fuses by retrieval score.

name: LongCat Sparse Attention (LSA) — streaming-aware, cross-layer, hierarchical lightning indexing

source.title: LongCat Sparse Attention: Taming the Lightning via Streaming-aware Hierarchical Indexing

oneLiner: Three fixes to lightning-indexer sparse attention: rewrite scattered selected KV into contiguous layouts, reuse selection across consecutive layers, coarse-to-fine scoring — the newest entry on the timeline (12 days before this page was written).
whyFootnote: Engineering refinements of the DSA-family indexer.

name: MiMo-V2-Flash — 5:1 sliding window (128) : global with a learnable attention-sink bias

source.title: MiMo-V2-Flash (Hugging Face); MiMo-V2-Flash Technical Report
source.evidence: HF repo created 2025-12-16T08:47:02Z; card: 'SWA layers use a window size of 128 tokens' at a '5:1 ratio', 'learnable attention sink bias'; report arXiv API published 2026-01-06T07:31:47Z (v1)

oneLiner: gpt-oss's 128-token banded layers and learned sink, plus Gemma's 5:1 ratio, in a 309B open MoE — the 2025 recipe restated by another lab.
